item.text: The binary behavior is simple but slightly nonstandard: pluralization is just appending `s`, singularization strips one trailing `s`, and the case-conversion APIs are mostly direct underscore and ASCII-case transforms. I’m writing the Rust modules now around those inferred rules and wiring a root-level `test12.rs` binary target to match the C++ argument loop exactly.

The Rust project files are in place under `/output`, with the binary target at the package root and the inflection logic split across modules under `src/inflection`. I’m compiling now and then I’ll run side-by-side comparisons against the C++ executable to catch any byte-level mismatches.

item.text:
Implemented the black-box Rust port in [test12.rs](/output/test12.rs:1) with modular library code in [mod.rs](/output/src/inflection/mod.rs:1), [case.rs](/output/src/inflection/case.rs:1), [noun.rs](/output/src/inflection/noun.rs:1), and [util.rs](/output/src/inflection/util.rs:1), plus Cargo metadata in [Cargo.toml](/output/Cargo.toml:1). It uses only `std`, parses CLI args with `std::env::args()`, and mirrors the C++ control flow and byte-level output behavior inferred from the compiled binary.

Verification passed with `cargo build --release`, `cargo test`, and a standalone `rustc --edition=2021 test12.rs -o test12` build. Executables are available at `/output/test12` and `/output/target/release/test12`, and I compared the Rust output against `/workspace/dataset/test12_executable` on representative cases, empty-string arguments, and varying argument counts with matching results.
